content.text: Xiaomeng, look! The designer just sent the first draft of the Shiba Inu's chibi-style character. Isn't it super cute? I specifically emphasized highlighting the "boss's" social butterfly vibe—you know, that energy from last time at the park when he was fetching the frisbee and rolling around on the grass, being all adorable! I think this chubby design goes really well with the yellow background. What do you think?

Wow, this design is so adorable! The combination of brown fur and a white face feels very warm, and the round head indeed gives off a lively vibe. It reminds me of how 'Boss' was socializing everywhere during the previous pet gathering, along with its viral moment of grinning at the camera. However, has the Ragdoll cat design been released yet? I'm a bit looking forward to a cool and aloof style, just like my blue-eyed long-haired cat that spends all day curled up on a blanket.

Don't rush, the Ragdoll cat is here too! Look at this little kitten, with its white body accented by light brown, fluffy fur, sitting quietly—doesn’t it perfectly capture the aloof elegance of your Ragdoll? I had the designer refer to the photo you sent earlier—the one where it was lying on a gray blanket, with such a serene vibe. I think this chibi version really captures its essence.

Oh my goodness, this design really hits the spot for me! The soft colors and fluffy tail perfectly capture the elegant temperament of a Ragdoll cat. Xingchen, the designer you found is truly amazing. These two images together—the outgoing Shiba Inu versus the aloof Ragdoll—create such an adorable contrast, just like the "Most Adorable Contrast Award" we envisioned when planning the pet social event. It also echoes the poster theme from that offline meetup, "Outgoing Shiba Inu vs. Aloof Ragdoll."

Haha, absolutely! As a creative planner at an advertising agency, I definitely have an eye for aesthetics—just like when I shared those game skins earlier, I could instantly tell which one was more dazzling: Lan's sci-fi style or the aesthetic style you prefer. But looks alone aren't enough; we need to see how it actually works when applied to the product. The designer also created a few sample images. Let me send them to you.

Okay, send it over quickly! I can hardly wait, especially since this is our first attempt at co-branded product development—we need to handle it with care. By the way, have you followed up further on the supplier suggestions you mentioned earlier? We need to consider the costs in advance, just like we did with the appreciation dinner gathering and the pet supplies group purchase—we have to act within our means.

First, take a look at this Shiba Inu avatar design. It would work well on scarves or small accessories—the cute smile and little tongue are sure to attract fans. It reminds me of that collaborative cat food ad I saw earlier featuring a Shiba Inu sticking out its tongue, which also followed this adorable style. I’ve made initial contact with the supplier, and the price seems reasonable, but it ultimately depends on the order quantity. Which do you think would be more popular—the chibi-style Shiba Inu or the Ragdoll?

Judging from fan feedback, both are quite popular! The Shiba Inu's outgoing personality feels more down-to-earth, while the Ragdoll's aloof style has a unique charm. However, if I had to choose, I think the Shiba Inu might appeal to a broader audience, especially since "Boss" has already gained some fame in the pet community—growing from a few thousand followers before the event to nearly fifty thousand, and that meme of him being ignored by a cat has even gone viral. But we can create a series of products to cater to both, just like when collecting game skins—you might prefer sci-fi styles, while I lean toward aesthetic ones, each appealing to different audiences.

That makes sense! Now, look at the design of this ceramic bowl—the patterns of dogs and cats are printed on it, making it very practical for daily use. I think fans would appreciate such everyday items. Just as we discussed earlier, collaborative products should balance fun and practicality—this aligns perfectly with your core value of "practical value." What do you think about tote bags?

The canvas bag is highly practical, suitable for daily commuting or shopping. With its beige background paired with cartoon patterns, the design is simple and bright, making it likely to be very popular. Xingchen, the sample image of this canvas bag you sent, with the dog and cat side by side, looks quite harmonious. It reminds me of the synergy we had when planning events together, and also of the 'Clean Plate' photo you took after our last dinner gathering, which captured the joyful and harmonious atmosphere.

Exactly! From gaming partners to event planning collaborators, and now working together on co-branded products, our partnership is getting deeper and deeper—just like how I comforted you when you lost five games in a row, then you became a top mid-laner, and now we’re organizing pet meetups and beginner script-killing sessions together, leveling up step by step! I suggest we start with ceramic bowls and canvas tote bags for our first product line—one for home, one for on-the-go, covering different scenarios. As for pricing, what do you think is appropriate? Let’s refer to our previous experience with group buys for pet supplies.

During group purchases, fans are quite sensitive to prices, but co-branded products carry design value, so they can be priced slightly higher. How about setting the ceramic bowl at 50-80 yuan and the tote bag at 30-50 yuan? This way, we can ensure profitability without making fans feel it's too expensive. We can start with a pre-sale to test the market response, similar to how we organize a 'friends and family beginner session' when inviting people for a script murder game—a small-scale trial. It's also like the previous game skin sharing, where everyone is always enthusiastic about new products.

Great idea! The pre-sale plan can be promoted by leveraging the fan community. You'll be in charge of community maintenance and user segmentation—just as meticulously as you did when building the pet fan community and establishing segmentation rules. I'll handle content creation, shooting some creative promotional videos—inspired by the last video "How to Achieve a Clean Plate Campaign at a Trendy Restaurant," this time we can showcase the product design process. As for production preparation, I'll contact suppliers for sampling, and you can help review the details?

No problem! I'll carefully check the materials and dimensions to ensure quality—after all, I have a "worry-prone nature," just like when I prepared risk plans and supply lists for offline events before. Additionally, we can set up pre-sale incentives, such as early bird discounts or limited-edition gifts, to encourage fan participation. This reminds me of the enthusiasm everyone has for new game skins when collecting them. We can draw inspiration from that marketing strategy, similar to how you attract viewers with your dramatic flair during live streams.

Haha, you're really getting the hang of operations! So it's settled: the first batch of products will be ceramic bowls and canvas bags, priced as you suggested. We'll launch the pre-sale through our community and divide the tasks for execution. Production preparations will start next week, aiming to go live within a month. This collaborative development might just become a new highlight for our pet IP—from the sudden idea of creating a social media account for "the boss" to the success of offline events, and now we're really about to release merchandise. Fun comes first!

Well, I have confidence too! From losing streaks in games to the success of pet events, and now to product development, we've been growing together all along. Xingchen, thank you for your creativity and encouragement, which have made these projects both fun and meaningful—just like you always say, 'reject boredom,' and I strive to maintain 'harmonious relationships.' Looking forward to seeing the fans' feedback!

Same to you! Your organizational skills and thoughtful suggestions always make things go more smoothly. Alright then, I'll go contact the suppliers for sampling, and you can prepare the community promotional materials. Let's stay in touch and keep each other updated on any progress—just like how efficient we were when planning events before. Who knows, maybe we can even organize a product launch themed party, similar to how we invited people for the script murder mystery.
